newsitem.title: FRANCE: Far-right French mayor axes theatre head.
newsitem.headline: Far-right French mayor axes theatre head.

text.p: Catherine Megret, the far-right mayor of Vitrolles, southern France, has axed the director of a municipal movie theatre for refusing to take a series of short films about homosexuality off the schedule.
The firing of Regine Juin, who had run the Les Lumieres cinema for 11 years, was the latest episode in a culture war being waged by the National Front in the four southern towns it controls.

Culture Minister Catherine Trautmann said the decision by Megret, wife of the Front's number two official Bruno Megret, was "disrespectful, unfair and marked by an ideology that fails to take into account the need for openness in film and other forms of culture".
"I know this person's good work promoting creative cinema and in favour of quality films and I will not let her down," Trautmann said.

France's four National Front mayors have had works and publications they judged too leftist or "multi-cultural", including the left-wing daily Liberation newspaper, removed from public libraries and replaced with others from the far-right.

They have also fought to eliminate special meals in school canteens for Moslem and Jewish children and to end subsidies for civic groups with ties to the Left and for rap music groups whose musicians are primarily of north African descent.
Catherine Megret was in court earlier this week in the southern city of Aix-en-Provence over a newspaper interview in which she has been charged with making racist insults.

Three anti-racism associations and more than 700 private citizens accused her of inciting racial hatred and discrimination in an interview with the German daily Berliner Zeitung, when she called immigrants "colonialists" and espoused racial inequality.
Bruno Megret called the trial a witch hunt and an infringement of freedom of speech.

The Front, which advocates sending immigrants home and rewriting the constitution to favour native-born French people in housing, jobs and education, consistently wins about 15 percent of the vote in nationwide elections. But it garners a larger share in the south and northeast.
